title: Build a thermostat in Model, View, Controller

task.text: Wire a thermostat so the model, the view and the controller each do one job and know the least possible.
`ModelListener` is given. Fill in the three skeletons.

items: `Thermostat` (model): `target()`; `adjust(int delta)` clamps the target to 10..30 and tells every listener the new target, even when it did not move.
`Controller(Thermostat, Consumer<String>)`: `onInput("up")` and `"down"` adjust by 1; anything else sends `Unknown: <text>` to the consumer.
The model knows no view or controller; the view never changes the model.

checks.title: Up and down adjust; others are reported
Input, model and view work together
The model knows neither view nor controller
The view only observes the model

hints.text: Ask of each class: what does it own, and what may it know? State and rules belong to the model. Showing belongs to the view. Translating input into model calls belongs to the controller.

The model keeps a `List<ModelListener>` and calls it after each `adjust`. `TextView` implements `ModelListener` and only writes to its `Consumer`. `Controller` holds the `Thermostat` and a `Consumer<String>` for errors.
